biography.plain_text: John Wallrock was a British insurance executive who chaired Minet Holdings, a major Lloyd’s broking group. He joined the board of PCW when Minet acquired the underwriting agency in 1973, becoming its sole board representative under an arrangement that left the agency’s founders in control. He left Minet in 1982.

long_biography.plain_text:
A model of HMS Victory began with an idea from John Wallrock, chairman of insurance broker J. H. Minet & Co. He proposed that brokerage firms give Lloyd’s a model, and helped arrange the commission through London’s Parker Gallery. The brokers’ association supported the project to mark the opening of administrative offices at Chatham.

Model-maker Philip Wride recreated the ship as it first went to sea, including stern galleries and a carved figurehead absent from its later appearance. Timber from Victory’s original lower gun deck went into the model, built with frames and planks. After temporary display in London, it was destined for the entrance hall at Gun Wharf.
